Download editable Excel template The Excel template starts with the same fictional example and editable dated events. Your browser inputs are not transferred into it. Excel formulas recalculate its base schedule. Review your inputs ↑ AI-generated editorial scene. All calculator and template example amounts are fictional. What this calculator includes Build thirteen seven-day periods from your selected start date. Enter up to 100 dated cash events with financing shown separately. Test operating receipt delays and collection reductions without changing payment dates. See minimum cash, reserve shortfall and events excluded from the horizon. Download your current CSV snapshot or a separate formula-driven Excel template. How to fill out a cash flow forecast template Choose a start date and reconciled available bank cash. Do not include undrawn borrowing or restricted deposits as spendable opening cash. List customer receipts on realistic expected collection dates rather than invoice or sale dates. Include cash tax received in the bank amount when applicable. List payroll, suppliers, rent, equipment, tax remittances and owner withdrawals on cash payment dates. Include withheld amounts and employer obligations once on their actual remittance dates. Keep loan or equity receipts and financing payments separate. They change cash but do not turn into operating sales. Do not include noncash depreciation as a payment. Review all thirteen weeks, especially the lowest balance and reserve shortfall. An empty future week means no events entered, not proof that the business has no expenses. Test a collection delay or lower collection percentage, then inspect excluded events. Download the snapshot or use the Excel template for a base forecast that recalculates when edited. 13-week cash flow forecast formulas Week 1 covers the selected start date through six days later. Each following week starts seven days after the previous start; the thirteenth week ends 90 days after the start date. Cash receipts = operating receipts + financing receipts. Cash payments = operating payments + financing payments. Net cash = receipts − payments. Closing cash = opening cash + net cash. Next week opening cash = previous week closing cash. Reserve headroom = closing cash − minimum reserve. Reserve funding shortfall = max(0, reserve − lowest of initial opening cash and thirteen weekly closing balances). This identifies the modeled funding floor, not an automatically approved credit line. Scenario operating receipt date = original cash date + delay days. Scenario operating receipt amount = entered amount × collection percentage ÷ 100. Payments and financing dates/amounts remain unchanged. A delayed receipt beyond week thirteen does not appear in the displayed cash totals. Worked forecast example: profitable work can still create a cash gap The base example opens with $12,000. Week 1 collects $9,000 and pays $8,000 payroll, closing at $13,000. Week 2 pays $7,000 suppliers and closes at $6,000. Week 3 collects $11,000 and pays a $2,000 financing repayment, closing at $15,000. Later weeks remain flat because the fictional schedule has no more events. With a $5,000 reserve, the base example stays above the floor. Add a 14-day operating receipt delay: week 1 closes at $4,000 and week 2 at −$3,000. The reserve funding shortfall is $8,000, even though the unchanged receipts eventually restore the closing balance. At 50% operating collections and no delay, total operating receipts fall to $10,000. The same $17,000 payments leave $5,000 closing cash. This is a collection assumption, not a probability or a bad-debt accounting entry. A receipt scheduled on the final day belongs to week thirteen. Moving it one day later removes it from the window; the exclusion warning explains the missing cash instead of silently extending the horizon. Free Excel template and CSV: choose the right download The current-scenario CSV includes your entered cash events, scenario settings and thirteen computed weekly rows. It contains snapshot values and does not recalculate after editing. Free spreadsheet applications can open it. The Excel download is a separate, editable base template with dated cash events and formulas for weekly receipts, payments, opening cash, closing cash and reserve headroom. It begins with fictional example values; replace them before using it. Its base schedule does not include the browser delay and collection controls. Keep the dated events tied to absolute dates when rolling forward. Reconcile actual bank cash, remove completed events, update unpaid receipts and payment dates, and enter the new opening balance. Changing the start date alone can exclude old events; it does not roll their dates forward. Review payment timing before arranging funding Confirm large customer receipts with the person who will pay. Contractual terms and DSO averages cannot establish an individual receipt date. Review daily transactions within a low-cash week. Weekly closing balances can hide payroll going out before a customer pays. Separate confirmed borrowing from a funding need. Add financing only when its amount and timing are plausible, then retain repayment dates. Refresh the forecast regularly with actual bank cash and newly confirmed dates. Use the separate runway tool for a stable monthly-burn estimate. Cash budget and cash receipts budget: bridge sales to bank dates A business cash budget is a dated schedule: opening available cash plus cash receipts minus cash payments equals closing cash. A cash receipts budget schedules expected collections by channel and payment date; it is not simply this month's recognized sales. Carry unpaid opening invoices, expected refunds and relevant deposits consistently. In a separate fictional week, opening cash $5,000 plus $3,000 collections less $4,000 payments closes at $4,000. If $1,000 of those collections slips to the next week, this week closes at $3,000; the later receipt must not be counted twice. An operating-profit budget and a cash budget need a bridge for settlement timing, inventory payments, noncash expenses and financing. This is business liquidity planning, not personal cash-envelope budgeting. Place the cash forecast inside the wider master budget The master budget connects operating plans, cash schedules and a projected balance sheet. This cash tool supports timing; it does not automatically produce the other statements. Master budget example and operating-to-cash bridge Verify opening cash and check the spreadsheet after import Before forecasting, summarize the last completed period and reconcile its closing cash on the same account basis. Carry that verified balance into the new forecast opening field. Keep already-cleared payments out of future events and move only outstanding collections to revised expected dates. Use “Download this scenario (CSV)” to keep the browser scenario as values, or choose the separate Excel template for an editable formula-driven base schedule. These downloads serve different purposes. For Google Sheets, upload a copy of the XLSX to Drive, open it with Google Sheets and save a converted copy if you intend to edit it there. Keep the original file for comparison. Before using imported results, confirm dates are recognized as dates, amounts are numeric and formulas reference the intended input cells. Check the opening-to-closing carry-forward in the weekly rows. Check a controlled copy against the fictional base example: $12,000 opening plus $20,000 receipts minus $17,000 payments gives $15,000 ending cash. Confirm the dated rows place the events in their intended weeks. Then replace every example event, review the full 13-week horizon and check reserve headroom. The workbook base schedule does not automatically inherit the browser’s delay or collection-percentage scenario. Check actual net cash flow and closing cash Follow the actual-to-forecast cutoff example The workbook download remains the existing XLSX. Native Google Sheets import and recalculation have not been independently verified in this review; the checks above are a verification procedure, not a compatibility certification. Assumptions and limits This is a direct cash forecast, not revenue recognition, net profit or a three-statement accounting model. Start from reconciled available cash and enter actual expected bank movements once. The two display categories distinguish financing from all other cash; they are not a statutory cash-flow classification statement. Scenario delay and collection percentage apply only to operating receipts; financing is unchanged. Events outside the date window are excluded and counted. Minimum cash considers opening and weekly closing balances, so an intraweek overdraft can still be missed. Negative cash does not create a loan facility. Frequently asked questions Is this cash flow forecast template free? Yes. The browser tool, CSV snapshot and editable Excel base template are free and require no account. Can I use the template in Excel or Google Sheets? The download is an XLSX workbook with ordinary formulas and a dated event schedule. It can be opened in Excel or imported into compatible spreadsheet applications. Check formulas and validation after import; the CSV is a values-only snapshot. Should I enter sales or cash collections? Enter money on the expected bank receipt date. A credit sale today that will be paid next month belongs on its expected collection date, not on today’s sale date. Does the forecast automatically repeat payroll or rent? No. Enter every expected dated payment. The example is deliberately short; a flat future week means no entered events, not no future obligations. Why is an event missing from the weekly table? Its original or delayed cash date may be before the start or after the thirteenth week. The tool reports how many events and how much adjusted cash were excluded. Review the dates and horizon. Can a positive week-end balance guarantee no overdraft? No. A payroll payment early in the week can precede a customer receipt later that week. Review the daily cash sequence when available cash is tight. Does changing currency convert my forecast? No. Currency selection only changes labels. A nominal 4.5% compounded monthly has 4.5939825% effective annual yield and produces about 10,459.40. The same printed percentage is not the same rate basis. What this calculator includes Two independently specified rate bases on an identical deposit and term Months/12 or actual entered days/365 planning convention Principal, gross interest, maturity difference and selected checkpoints Local CSV snapshot and print; no account opening, market quotes or saved entries Compare the same funded amount and term Enter the amount deposited. Keep account-opening fees or other cash needs outside this gross model. Zero deposit is a deliberate zero result, not a missing input. Choose whole months or whole days and a matching term for both alternatives. A zero term returns principal with no modeled growth. For each alternative, identify whether the document states APY or a nominal annual interest rate. Only nominal rates need a compounding frequency. Read maturity value and interest separately. Compare access, renewal, fees, provider details and disclosure terms before acting. Download a local scenario snapshot or print the model. Reconcile its assumptions with the actual provider record; it is not a quoted offer. The rate basis changes the growth factor For an entered APY Y as a decimal and modeled years t, gross maturity = P × (1+Y)^t. For nominal annual rate r with n compounds per year, effective annual yield = (1+r/n)^n − 1. The tool then applies that equivalent annual yield over the same t. This avoids applying an APY as if it were a nominal periodic rate. The APY choice ignores the frequency selector because effective annual yield already expresses annual compounding. The nominal choice uses annual, semiannual, quarterly, monthly or 365-times compounding. Days/365 is an explicit model convention, not a claim that every institution uses the same posting rules. Gross interest is maturity minus the original deposit. The comparison difference is B maturity minus A maturity at the same modeled date; it does not value liquidity restrictions or deduct tax and charges. Amounts display to two decimal places, while the model retains precision. A checked fictional comparison Use a 10,000 deposit and twelve modeled months. Alternative A states 4.5% APY. Its maturity is 10,000 × 1.045 = 10,450; gross interest is 450. Alternative B states a nominal annual rate of 4.5%, compounded monthly. Its maturity is 10,000 × (1+0.045/12)^12 = 10,459.3982504…, or 10,459.40 displayed. B’s effective annual yield is approximately 4.5939825%, so its gross maturity is 9.40 higher in this defined example. No extra deposit, fee, tax or withdrawal is included. This comparison isolates rate convention; it does not demonstrate that any real account is available or suitable. If both alternatives use 4.5% APY with the same principal and term, the modeled maturity values agree regardless of any nominal-frequency selector. At zero rate, maturity equals principal for any supported term. A six-month APY model uses a square-root annual growth factor rather than simply halving one year’s compound return. Read the deposit record before relying on a projection A deposit certificate’s maturity date, interest-crediting policy, fixed or variable rate terms and access conditions determine what actually happens. Review the institution, account ownership and written disclosures. A calculator cannot establish deposit-insurance coverage or the consequences of holding multiple accounts. If interest is paid out rather than retained, those payments do not compound inside the same deposit as this model assumes. Brokered CDs can have different payout and sale arrangements. Use the contract’s cash-flow schedule instead of forcing an account with distributed interest into a retained-interest model. An early-exit penalty is not modeled by subtracting an arbitrary number of months of interest. Contracts can define the penalty base and interest period differently, and an early withdrawal also shortens the growth period. Obtain the actual terms and compare cash at the actual exit date. A larger maturity balance is only one part of the decision Match the term to the date funds may be needed. A higher modeled balance at maturity does not make money available for an earlier payroll, supplier bill or equipment payment. Keep a dated cash reserve and near-term obligations separate from money that can remain deposited. A long-term deposit can also expose the plan to reinvestment uncertainty at maturity and an opportunity cost if other available uses change. This page does not compare live offers or predict future rates. Run only rates you can document and label any what-if assumptions clearly. For a business decision, a deposit yield and project return answer different questions. Customer demand, operating contribution, capacity, taxes and funding dates can change an expansion case. Follow the connected expansion and valuation guides rather than interpreting this interest difference as a complete investment decision. Keep a reviewable comparison Record the source date, entered amount, rate label, compounding convention, term unit and any excluded fees beside your calculation. Print or download each version when assumptions change. A CSV download is a fixed snapshot, not an editable recalculating model. The checkpoint table divides the modeled term into twelve intervals. Its observation times can be fractional months or days; it does not claim that interest was actually credited at those points. A zero term contains only the opening observation. Method references were checked November 17, 2026. The fictional calculations are independent teaching examples. Provider documents and applicable rules control a real account; no recommendation to buy a particular deposit is generated. Assumptions and limits Fixed nonnegative entered rates, one opening deposit and retained interest throughout the term. No fees, tax, further deposits, early withdrawal, rate changes or cash-paid interest. Months are modeled as months/12 years; days use days/365. Fractional compounding intervals use smooth equivalent growth, which may differ from a provider’s actual crediting/day-count rules. Checkpoints are model observations, not bank statements. This is not an account-disclosure calculation, product recommendation, availability check or insurance determination. Inputs reset on reload; downloads contain only the scenario you request. Frequently asked questions Does the calculator use current CD rates? No. Every rate is entered by you. The starting rates are fictional teaching assumptions, not current offers. Should I enter APY or nominal interest? Use the label on the provider document. APY already describes effective annual yield; nominal interest needs its compounding convention. Can I add monthly deposits? Not in this fixed-opening-deposit model. Use the linked Future Value calculator for recurring contributions. Are tax and early-withdrawal penalties included? No. This is gross retained-interest growth. Review actual charges and cash dates separately. Are the checkpoints actual interest credits? No. They are observations of the equivalent-growth model, not a provider posting schedule. Does the higher result identify the better account? No. Availability, access, fees, terms, provider and coverage require a separate review. documents.text: DEPOSIT MATH · FREE · NO SIGNUP APY Calculator Convert a nominal annual interest rate to APY, reverse the calculation, or annualize a defined interest amount. This rate tool does not project a savings balance or compare live accounts. Your rate conversion Fictional example. Enter documented assumptions; this page supplies no current rates. Amounts use USD labels without conversion. Conversion method Nominal interest to APY APY to nominal interest Annualize principal and term interest Term mode is not an average-daily-balance statement calculation. Nominal annual interest (%) 0–100%; frequency is required. Compounds per year Annually Semiannually Quarterly Monthly Daily (365) Used for nominal/effective conversion; it does not change term annualization. Reset fictional example Inputs remain in this tab and reset on reload. Nothing is submitted to a bank or stored by this calculator. Rate conversion result Effective annual yield (APY) 4.593983 % Equivalent nominal annual rate 4.5 % 12 compounds per year Download scenario CSV Print / save PDF CSV exports are fixed snapshots, not recalculating spreadsheets. APY = [(1 + nominal decimal rate / compounds)^compounds − 1] × 100%. Reverse with compounds × [(1 + APY decimal)^(1 / compounds) − 1] × 100%. AI-created editorial illustration. Rates and numerical examples are fictional assumptions, not current offers. Check the fictional example A nominal annual 4.5% rate compounded monthly corresponds to approximately 4.5939825% APY. A quoted 4.5% APY corresponds to approximately 4.4097713% nominal annual interest with monthly compounding. What this calculator includes Nominal-to-effective and effective-to-nominal conversion Separate opening-principal and term-interest annualization mode Explicit supported compounding frequencies and rate boundaries Transparent formulas, fictional cases and local CSV snapshot Choose the rate question before entering a number Choose nominal interest to APY when the document gives a nominal annual rate and a compounding frequency. Choose APY to nominal when you have an effective annual yield and need the equivalent nominal rate for a stated frequency. Use principal-and-interest annualization only for a defined opening principal and term with no intervening cash flows. Enter whole days and an interest amount, not a percentage. Read APY and nominal interest as different labels. Neither is an automatically available bank offer or a borrowing APR. Keep the written rate source and terms with a printed or downloaded snapshot. Convert a periodic growth factor, not just a label Let r be nominal annual interest as a decimal and n the number of compounds per year. APY = [(1+r/n)^n − 1] × 100%. For APY Y as a decimal, the equivalent nominal annual rate is n × [(1+Y)^(1/n) − 1] × 100%. Inputs and displayed outputs are percentages; the engine converts them to decimals once. At zero interest both results are zero. With annual compounding, nominal annual interest and APY agree. With positive nominal interest and more than one compound per year, APY exceeds that nominal rate because retained interest also earns interest. The magnitude depends on the rate and frequency; it is not a fixed add-on. The nominal-rate input supports 0–100%; APY input supports 0–1,000%. Frequencies are 1, 2, 4, 12 or 365 per year. These are numerical model limits, not statements about available product rates. Invalid or blank input produces a visible correction message instead of silently becoming zero. A checked fictional nominal-rate example At a nominal annual rate of 4.5%, compounded monthly, each monthly factor is 1+0.045/12 = 1.00375. Raising this factor to twelve and subtracting one gives 0.04593982504…, or 4.593982504…% APY. This is a fictional chosen rate and not a current market quote. Reverse the question: a 4.5% APY with monthly compounding has an equivalent nominal annual rate of 12 × [(1.045)^(1/12) − 1] = approximately 4.4097713%. The two displayed 4.5% labels therefore imply different equivalent rates. Use unrounded conversions when checking a round trip; rounded screen values can create tiny differences. The annualization mode asks a different input question. A fixed opening principal of 10,000 and 450 interest over 365 days produces a 4.5% annualized yield. Over a 182-day term, the same 450 interest annualizes to [(1+450/10,000)^(365/182) − 1] × 100%, approximately 9.229% before display rounding. The interest amount and day count must describe the same term. Keep opening-principal annualization separate from statement yield The term mode uses a beginning principal and the total interest earned on that unchanged principal over a defined term, assuming retained interest and no other transactions. The annualized result is a rate comparison, not an extra amount of cash actually received during the shorter term. A periodic statement can involve changing balances. The regulatory annual percentage yield earned calculation can use average daily balance under specified rules, which is not the opening-principal input on this page. Do not enter a closing balance or an average balance as opening principal merely to reproduce a statement percentage. Account disclosures can also have special rules for tiered or stepped rates, certain longer-term accounts, required interest withdrawals and maturity conventions. The CFPB reference explains these distinctions. This educational calculator does not replace an institution’s required disclosure process. APY is not a shortcut for a loan APR This tool converts deposit-style interest and effective yield. A borrowing APR can reflect a loan’s timing and included finance charges under applicable rules. You cannot turn a lender’s fee-inclusive APR into a deposit return merely by using the same percentage field. Likewise, the result does not deduct bank fees, tax, withdrawal costs or inflation. A high gross APY can coexist with a lower realized cash benefit after those items. Record each excluded item separately rather than calling the converted rate an after-tax or fee-adjusted yield. An investment’s uncertain return is also not a promised APY. The linked Future Value calculator handles entered growth scenarios with a separate contribution schedule; it does not make an assumed return guaranteed. Keep historical observations, hypothetical rates and contractual disclosures clearly labeled. Record the basis before comparing alternatives Keep the provider’s exact rate label, source date, compounding convention, balance conditions, applicable term and access restrictions. Comparing percentages without these records can put unlike products on the same line. A rate conversion only resolves the mathematical convention you specify. Use the CD calculator when the question is how much a fixed opening deposit grows to at maturity. Use Future Value when the question includes recurring contributions. Use business ROI when the question concerns project cash costs and benefits. Keeping those intents separate prevents a deposit-rate quotient from becoming a business profitability claim. The method references were checked November 17, 2026. Printed results and CSV exports are snapshots of your entered assumptions. The page stores inputs only in its current browser state and does not open accounts, submit applications or supply current rates. Assumptions and limits Conversion assumes a constant nonnegative nominal rate and stated compounds per year, or an entered effective annual APY. The separate earned-interest mode assumes a fixed opening principal, retained interest, no intervening deposits/withdrawals and whole actual entered days; it uses a 365-day annualization basis. It is not the average-daily-balance periodic-statement method and does not cover all Regulation DD exceptions, tiers, stepped rates, distributed interest or product-specific terms. No market-rate feed, account recommendation, tax or fee calculation. Reloading clears entries. Frequently asked questions Is APY the same as nominal interest? They agree with annual compounding. With positive interest and more frequent retained-interest compounding, effective APY is higher than the nominal annual rate. Can I convert APY back to a nominal rate? Yes. Select APY to nominal and choose the compounding frequency for the equivalent nominal annual rate. Is this a loan APR calculator? No. It does not model borrowing finance charges, loan payments or fee-inclusive APR disclosures. Can I enter interest earned over part of a year? Yes, in the separate term mode, with fixed opening principal, whole days and no intervening deposits or withdrawals. Does term mode reproduce every statement APY? No. Periodic-statement yield can use average daily balances and product-specific rules that are outside this opening-principal model. Where do I calculate a maturity balance? Use the linked CD calculator for fixed-term deposit growth, or Future Value for recurring contributions. Full monthly rent Rent only; exclude deposits, utilities, fees and taxes. First charged date Last charged date Both selected dates are charged. Use one calendar month; split a multi-month period into separate calculations. Day-rate basis Actual calendar-month days Fixed 30 divisor (actual charged-day count) Annual rent ÷ 365 (monthly × 12) Confirm the agreement’s day-count and rounding rules. These comparisons do not decide which charge is legally due. Reset fictional example Prorated rent comparison $900.00 Actual calendar-month days Charged calendar days, both dates included 15 Actual days in this month 30 Selected daily rate (rounded for display only) $60.00 Calculated as unrounded daily rate × charged days; final amount rounds once to cents. Do not multiply the displayed rounded daily rate. Same occupied dates; different rate conventions Basis Divisor Charge Actual calendar-month days 30 $900.00 Fixed 30 divisor 30 $900.00 Annualized 365 divisor 365; annual rent = monthly × 12 $887.67 A fixed 30 divisor applied to 31 actual days can exceed one month’s rent. Annualized 365 always uses 365 even in leap years. Neither alternative implements a contractual 30/360 date-adjustment convention. Download values CSV Print / save PDF CSV includes input scope, dates or income period and precise calculation values. It does not contain formulas or save a scenario to an account. AI-generated editorial illustration with topic text; not a customer record or verified financial document. What this calculator includes Inclusive start/end dates validated against the real calendar, including leap February. Actual-month, fixed30 and annual365 arithmetic compared on the same charged days. Unrounded daily arithmetic and final two-decimal rounding, with a visible calculation trail. Tab-only inputs, currency labels, values CSV, reset and print. Define which dates are actually charged Proration starts with an agreed billing interval. Enter the first charged day and last charged day, not simply a key-collection date or a convenient moving date. This calculator includes both endpoints. A period from November 16 through November 30 contains 15 charged calendar days; subtracting date numbers without adding the first day would give 14 and understate this interval. If the agreement excludes the final day, enter the last day actually charged. A move-out date alone does not establish the last billable date or eliminate a notice obligation. This arithmetic page cannot decide those contractual questions. Record the agreement, agreed method and any relevant professional confirmation alongside the downloaded result. The tool accepts a single calendar month so the actual-month divisor is unambiguous. A period spanning November and December needs separate runs, each using its own dates and full-month rent. Add the separately rounded charges only under the rounding policy being used. A rent increase during the period also needs a separate segment, even if the dates share a month. Compare explicit daily-rate conventions Actual-month charge = full monthly rent ÷ actual calendar days in that month × charged days. Fixed 30 charge = monthly rent ÷ 30 × actual charged days. Annual 365 charge = monthly rent × 12 ÷ 365 × charged days. These are three defined arithmetic choices, not a declaration that all leases permit each one. No live local-law rule selects a method for you. For the loaded fictional 1800 rent and November 16–30 interval, actual-month and fixed 30 both give 900. The annualized comparison gives 887.6712328767… before final rounding to 887.67. The difference comes from the rate basis, not from different occupancy dates. Preserve the method in your records rather than selecting whichever result happens to be cheaper. A full 31-day December at 1800 monthly rent gives 1800 under actual-month days, 1860 under the fixed 30 divisor and 1834.52 under annual 365. A comparison above one month’s rent is not an error in this defined fixed-divisor arithmetic; it highlights why the relevant agreement and billing convention matter. Fixed 30 does not silently change the charged date count to 30. Round the final amount, not each displayed day For an original fictional 1700 rent in a 31-day month, 12 charged days give 1700÷ 31 × 12 = 658.064516…which rounds to 658.06. The displayed daily amount of 54.84 is not reused in the calculation; 54.84× 12 would give 658.08. Rounding the intermediate rate would add two cents in this example. The values CSV retains the unrounded daily rate and calculation result as text values alongside the rounded amount. It contains no formulas, so editing a date in that file does not recalculate the bill. The tool uses two-decimal monetary display for consistent teaching even when the selected currency normally uses another minor-unit convention; confirm invoicing precision separately. Check February and leap-year boundaries In fictional February 2028, a 2900 monthly rent charged from February 15 through February 29 covers 15 of 29 days. Actual-month arithmetic gives 1500. Fixed 30 gives 1450, and annual 365 gives 1430.14. The annual 365 comparison deliberately keeps 365 as its chosen denominator; it does not become 366 in leap years. Invalid dates such as February 30 are rejected. So are reversed dates, missing required amounts, unsupported date formats and cross-month intervals. Zero rent is accepted as an explicit zero scenario. A same-day interval counts one charged day. The tool does not infer free days from a missing date. Reconcile the result with the complete payment record A partial rent charge is not the entire move-in payment. List refundable deposits, utility charges, administrative fees, taxes, credits and any other contractual amounts separately. Do not reduce the daily rent rate by a deposit or add a monthly charge twice. This page intentionally does not total those items because their treatment needs the agreement’s own records. Compare the entered monthly rent with the signed schedule and make sure a weekly amount has not been pasted into a monthly field. Keep the rent period and cash-payment date separate: a payment made today can cover a future interval. If this is part of a business cash plan, enter its actual due date in the 13-week cash forecast rather than treating the prorated charge as a whole-month expense automatically. Method sources and related planning HUD’s model-lease instructions provide a program-specific example of dividing tenant rent by actual month days and multiplying by occupied days. That document is not a universal private-lease rule and is not an endorsement of this site. California DOT’s published proration examples also illustrate a daily-rate-times-days calculation with final-cent rounding in their own program context. The fixed 30 and annual 365 comparisons here are explicitly stated teaching conventions. They are not copied lease terms or jurisdictional advice. For wider planning, separate gross earnings from take-home pay, compare the selected debt-to-income scope, or build a dated cash forecast. gross earnings from take-home pay selected debt-to-income scope cash forecast Assumptions and limits One calendar month, both selected dates charged. Calendar arithmetic only: the tool does not determine entitlement, required notice, local law, lease interpretation or a legal invoice. Confirm the agreed date count and rate basis. Fixed 30 uses actual charged days divided by 30 and is not a 30/360 day-adjustment method. Annual 365 uses monthly rent × 12 / 365 even in leap years. Deposits, utilities, fees, rent changes, taxes and credits are excluded. Rent is nonnegative up to 1 trillion; dates 1900–9999. Required blanks are incomplete, not zero. Currency labels do not convert amounts. Money displays two decimals; final charge rounds once from 40-digit decimal arithmetic. Frequently asked questions Does this calculator include both dates? Yes. The first and last charged dates are both included. November 16–30 is 15 days. Enter the actual last charged day if an agreement excludes a move-out date. Which rent-proration method is legally correct? This tool does not decide that. Confirm the agreement, applicable rules and required date/rounding policy. The displayed methods are defined arithmetic comparisons, not universal legal standards. Can I calculate a period crossing two months? Run each calendar month separately with its own dates and monthly rent. The calculator rejects cross-month entries so it cannot silently apply one month’s divisor to another. Why can fixed 30 give more than a full month’s rent? The fixed 30 comparison divides by 30 but still counts actual charged days. A 31-dayinterval therefore uses 31/30 ofmonthly rent. It is not a 30/360 date-adjustment convention. How is leap-year February handled? The actual-month basis uses 29 days in a leap February. Annual 365 keeps its expressly chosen 365-daydenominator, even in a leap year. Does the CSV save or recalculate my lease? No. It downloads input and result values only. There is no account saving, bank connection, lease storage or recalculating spreadsheet formula. Start with a defined monthly debt-to-income ratio Debt-to-income arithmetic compares monthly payment obligations with monthly gross income. Add the payments included in the chosen scope, divide by gross monthly income and multiply by 100. The CFPB explains that lenders and loan products can have different limits. A number alone does not establish approval, an offered rate or the amount someone can safely spend. This calculator deliberately exposes its housing switch. When selected, total payments include the housing bundle plus other entered obligations. When unselected, the displayed total excludes housing, while the separate housing-only ratio stays visible. These are different scopes, not a financial improvement caused by toggling a box. Confirm the definitions needed for the actual comparison. For a mortgage-oriented comparison, the housing bundle may include principal, interest, property taxes, insurance and association charges where applicable. Enter each amount once; an escrow payment can already include tax or insurance. Rent may be treated differently by other DTI exercises. The tool does not prescribe a universal inclusion rule. Reproduce the original fictional payment case The loaded example uses 6000 gross monthly income and monthly payments of 1500 housing, 350 auto, 200 student, 150 credit-card minimums and 0 other. Total selected payments are 2200. The selected ratio is 2200÷ 6000 × 100 = 36.666666…%, displayed to four decimal places as 36.6667%. Housing alone is 1500÷ 6000 × 100 = 25%. Excluding the housing bundle leaves 700 of other payments and 11.6667% against the same gross income. That lower percentage answers a narrower question. It does not mean the household stopped paying housing, gained spending cash or qualified for a different loan. Record the switch setting alongside any shared result. Use required monthly payments rather than outstanding loan balances. A 20000 auto balance is not the same as a 350 monthly installment. For revolving credit, obtain the payment amount required for the comparison rather than assuming the full statement balance or last voluntary overpayment is the minimum obligation. Convert income periods without confusing pay schedules Annual income is divided by 12. Weekly pay is multiplied by 52 and divided by 12. Every-two-week pay uses 26 payments per year, while twice-monthly pay uses 24. These are annualized equivalents; the tool does not place paydays on a calendar or model a particular year containing an extra payday. In a separate fictional frequency example, 2400 every two weeks becomes 5200 per month, while 2400 twice monthly becomes 4800. Against 2200 selected payments, those denominators produce 42.3077% and 45.8333%. Treating the two schedules as identical would change the ratio even with unchanged debt. Use gross pay before employee taxes and deductions, not the net bank deposit. For self-employment or variable income, do not paste gross business sales into personal qualifying income. The applicable lender may use documentation and adjustments this simple calculator does not perform. The gross-pay-versus-net-pay guide explains the payroll boundary; business net income is a different record. gross-pay-versus-net-pay guide business net income Test an added payment and a chosen percentage separately Entering an additional 300 monthly payment in the base example gives 2500 total and 41.6667%. This scenario retains every existing obligation. A refinance, payoff or replacement needs the old payment removed through a deliberate new base scenario; adding the new loan while retaining the old payment would double count a replacement. The separate mortgage refinance calculator owns term, fees and same-horizon comparisons. If a user independently chooses 40% as a comparison percentage, 6000× 40% − 2200 = 200 of arithmetic payment headroom. This example is not a recommended limit, lender threshold or borrowing allowance. Adding 300 would exceed that chosen payment budget by 100. The result does not account for living expenses, taxes, emergency costs or cash timing. A blank optional additional-payment field means no scenario was requested. An explicit zero checks a zero change. A blank comparison field disables headroom; zero is a real chosen percentage and can produce negative headroom. A negative difference is retained rather than presented as zero available credit. mortgage refinance calculator Prepare source records before interpreting the percentage Use the same applicant or household scope for numerator and denominator. Do not include a second person’s income while omitting their relevant obligations, or count a shared debt twice. Write down how irregular income, support payments, deferred loans and housing were treated. The software cannot verify the completeness of supplied records. Compare current income documentation with current debt statements and the housing cost schedule. Keep groceries, utilities, transport, savings and other living costs in a separate cash budget even when they are outside the selected DTI numerator. A low selected ratio can coexist with a tight take-home cash position. Debt can exceed entered monthly gross income, so results above 100% are allowed and visibly flagged. Zero debt with positive income gives 0%; zero income cannot support a meaningful finite percentage and is rejected. Negative, missing required or nonfinite amounts do not become silent zeros. Use the result as a transparent record, not an approval The CFPB’s definition supports monthly debt divided by gross monthly income and explains that product/lender limits differ. The original cases here document this calculator’s chosen scope and arithmetic; they do not reproduce a lender decision or use a recommended pass/fail band. No external scoring service receives the values. Download the values CSV to retain the income frequency, housing switch, every entered payment, optional scenario and precise calculated values. Editing it does not recalculate formulas. Inputs stay in the tab and are not added to an account. For employer-side costs rather than employee take-home income, use the separate loaded employee cost calculator. A partial-month rent calculation is likewise a separate charge calculation, not a substitute for a monthly DTI payment basis. loaded employee cost calculator partial-month rent calculation Assumptions and limits Educational selected-obligation ratio, not a credit decision, affordability certificate, mortgage quote, legal definition or lender-specific underwriting model. Use gross income for the chosen period and monthly payment amounts, not balances. Housing inclusion is explicit; lender and product treatment of rent, mortgages, tax, insurance, support, deferred debts and income can differ. No approval thresholds or live rates are supplied. Proposed payment adds to retained obligations and does not replace a refinance payment. Gross income must be positive; amounts 0–1 trillion, chosen comparison 0–100%. Required blanks are incomplete, optional blank means not supplied. Currency labels do not convert. Ratios may exceed 100%. Values preserve 40-digit decimal calculation precision; displayed ratios up to 4 decimals. Frequently asked questions Does DTI use gross income or take-home pay? The denominator here is gross income before employee deductions, converted to a monthly equivalent. Do not use business sales as personal qualifying income or assume a lender will accept an undocumented amount. Is rent always included in DTI? No universal inclusion rule is imposed here. The housing switch defines this selected arithmetic scope. Confirm the relevant lender or product definitions; housing-only and housing-excluded results remain clearly labelled. Should I enter balances or monthly payments? Enter the monthly payment amount required for your comparison, such as an installment or credit-cardminimum, not the outstanding debt balance. What DTI percentage guarantees loan approval? None is provided by this calculator. Lenders and products differ, and approval also depends on information outside this model. An optional user-chosen percentage is only a mathematical comparison. Does an additional payment replace my existing mortgage? No. It adds to every retained obligation. For a replacement scenario, deliberately revise the base payments and check all relevant loan costs separately. Why is every-two-week income different from twice monthly? The annualized conventions use 26 payments for every two weeks and 24 for twice monthly. At 2400 perpayment, the monthly equivalents are 5200 and 4800. What this calculator includes Fixed-rate, fully amortizing monthly loan payment. Separate property tax, homeowners insurance, mortgage insurance and HOA. Unrounded amortization with a final payment that clears the balance. Download every monthly principal, interest and balance value as CSV. Calculate a fixed-rate mortgage payment Loan principal equals home price less down payment. For monthly rate i and n monthly payments, principal-and-interest payment M = P × i ÷ [1 − (1 + i)^−n]. At zero interest, M = P ÷ n. The annual note rate is divided by 12; APR includes other borrowing costs and is not substituted here. For each month, interest equals opening principal × monthly rate. The remainder of the loan payment reduces principal. Calculations retain precision; figures display to cents and the last payment clears the exact remaining balance. Actual lender schedules can differ because of daily accrual, rounding or payment dates. Reproduce the fictional example A $350,000 price less $70,000 down leaves $280,000 principal. At an assumed 6.5% fixed annual note rate over 30 years, monthly principal and interest are $1,769.79. Annual property tax $4,200 and annual homeowners insurance $1,800 add $350 and $150 per month. With $0 mortgage insurance and $100 HOA, the total monthly ownership budget is $2,369.79. These are inputs, not current rates or local cost benchmarks. For a separate zero-rate check, $120,000 over 10 years requires $1,000 principal per month, $0 interest and a zero balance after 120 payments. Adding ownership costs does not change amortization or the loan’s interest total. Loan payment, escrow and ownership costs are different Principal and interest are the loan-payment component. The lender payment may also collect tax and insurance through escrow and include mortgage insurance. HOA is often paid separately; it is included here only in the broader ownership budget. Do not enter insurance twice. The full ownership budget can also need maintenance, utilities, closing costs and other charges outside this tool. Taxes and insurance can change even when the principal-and-interest payment stays fixed. This model does not automatically cancel mortgage insurance or estimate approval, home appreciation, tax deductions or refinance savings. Use the right tool for the next question Compare an existing loan with a refinance at the same exit date Check a separately defined debt-to-income ratio Understand fee recovery versus refinance economic cost Assumptions and limits Educational fixed-rate monthly amortization. Inputs stay in this browser tab. No live quotes, approval, affordability determination, tax advice or lender endorsement. No extra payments, variable rates, balloon structures, daily accrual or fee-financing model. Ownership-cost assumptions stay constant; loan-payment totals exclude those separate costs. Frequently asked questions Does this show the whole monthly housing cost? It shows principal and interest plus your entered tax, insurance, mortgage insurance and HOA. Maintenance, utilities and closing costs remain outside the displayed budget. Should I use APR or the note rate? Enter the annual fixed note rate. APR incorporates additional borrowing costs and is not the periodic interest rate used by this amortization formula. Are the default rates current mortgage offers? No. All default amounts and rates are fictional planning inputs. Obtain current written quotes and property-specific estimates separately. Does a zero interest rate work? Yes. The loan principal is divided evenly across the scheduled number of monthly payments. Does mortgage insurance stop automatically? No. The entered monthly amount remains constant. Cancellation depends on your loan, servicing and applicable requirements. Is this the same as the refinance calculator? No. This calculates an original fixed-rate payment and ownership budget. The refinance tool compares an existing loan and replacement financing, costs and remaining balances at a common exit date. What this calculator includes US Etsy Payments fee breakdown with separate sales tax treatment 12% or 15% attributed Offsite Ads with the $100 order cap Separate models for shipped products and digital downloads Break-even and target item prices, with an ad-free comparison How Etsy seller fees are calculated Start with the item price after seller discounts, then add what you charge for shipping and any gift wrapping. For this US example, Etsy calculates the 6.5% transaction fee on that amount. Etsy Payments charges 3% plus $0.25 on the modeled checkout total, including applicable sales tax. Buyer tax is kept out of your revenue. Allocate $0.20 per listing charge. A new listing or renewal can incur a charge independently of a sale. If unsold listings or renewals are material, spread those related costs across expected sales instead of treating every order as a single charge. On an attributed Offsite Ads order, choose the rate Etsy applies to your shop. The modeled fee is 12% or 15% of seller revenue, limited to $100 per order. The calculator compares the same order with and without attribution so you can see what the ad costs. Worked example: a $40 Etsy order with paid shipping Fictional US order at 8% effective sales tax and 15% attributed Offsite Ads Order line Calculation Amount Seller revenue $40 item + $5 shipping $45.00 Buyer checkout $45 + $3.60 tax $48.60 Listing charge 1 × $0.20 $0.20 Transaction fee $45 × 6.5% $2.93 Payment processing $48.60 × 3% + $0.25 $1.71 Offsite Ads $45 × 15% $6.75 Seller costs $12 item + $6 postage + $2 supplies + $1 allowance $21.00 Contribution $45 less modeled fees and costs $12.42 Before Offsite Ads, the same order leaves $19.17. For a $20 contribution with the ad assumption unchanged, raise the item price to at least $50.08 in this model. The calculation retains fee precision before displaying cents, so the independently rounded table entries can differ from the total by a cent. Calculate profit on an Etsy digital download Choose Digital product for a printable, template or similar downloadable item. Buyer-paid shipping, postage and packaging are zero. Enter royalties or delivery costs per order and a support or unrecovered refund allowance. To recover a one-time design cost, divide it by a realistic number of sales and include it once in the unit cost. A fictional $12 printable with 8% effective buyer sales tax, one $0.20 listing charge, no attributed ad and $2.50 in seller costs leaves $7.88 in modeled contribution. The buyer pays $12.96. The 6.5% transaction fee uses the $12 item revenue and the payment processing fee uses the $12.96 checkout total. Price a handmade item when shipping or advertising changes Audit two recent payment-account orders. Compare your buyer shipping charge with the actual label and check which sale was attributed to Offsite Ads. Enter materials and paid making time in landed item cost. Enter packaging, postage and expected unrecovered returns once each. Test a buyer-paid shipping order and a free shipping offer. With free shipping, set the buyer charge to zero and leave the postage you pay in costs. Compare attributed and unattributed contribution. Use your actual expected order mix to decide whether the price can fund monthly overhead. Reconcile Etsy proceeds before changing your prices Match a single order to the listing, transaction, payment and Offsite Ads entries on its statement. Deposit timing, subscription charges, Etsy Ads spend and other account-level adjustments belong in the monthly plan. If an order is refunded, check which fees were credited and how much stock was recovered. Use the unrecovered amount to estimate the average loss per completed sale. Keep that estimate separate from the order subtotal. Assumptions and limits One domestic US Etsy item with USD settlement and Etsy Payments. Use the effective tax on item plus buyer-paid shipping, keeping the same effective rate in price scenarios. The model excludes currency conversion, taxes on fees, Etsy Ads campaign spend, refunds and separate account adjustments unless you enter an appropriate cost allowance. Contribution is before overhead and income tax. Frequently asked questions How much does Etsy take from a $40 sale? With $5 buyer-paid shipping and 8% effective sales tax, this example has $4.83 in modeled fees before Offsite Ads. An attributed 15% ad adds $6.75. Shipping and sales tax can change the fee bases. Does the Etsy calculator support digital downloads? Yes. Choose Digital product to exclude shipping, postage and packaging while keeping the listing, transaction, Etsy Payments and applicable Offsite Ads fees. Use the effective buyer tax shown for your order. Does Etsy charge fees on shipping? For this US model, shipping charged to the buyer enters the transaction, payments and applicable Offsite Ads fee bases. Your actual postage is a separate seller cost. What is the Etsy Offsite Ads cap? The modeled fee is capped at $100 per attributed order. Select the 12% or 15% rate shown by Etsy for your shop. Use zero for an unattributed order. Can I use the break-even price as my final listing price? It covers the entered fees and direct costs. Add a target contribution to fund overhead and owner pay, then compare the result with actual statement fees and buyer demand. What this calculator includes Selected US basic category schedules and a verified custom flat-rate mode $0.30 or $0.40 order charge based on checkout total Itemized final value, insertion and attributed General campaign fees Break-even and target item prices that account for the per-order fee cutoff How eBay final value fees are calculated For the supported basic schedules, the percentage applies to the item price, modeled buyer shipping and sales tax. Apply the selected category rate to the first $7,500 per item, then 2.35% to the portion above it. The custom option uses a single flat rate and does not apply a tier. The model adds $0.30 per order at a checkout total of $10 or less and $0.40 above $10. Sales tax can move a sale above that cutoff even if the item price alone stays below it. Seller revenue excludes buyer tax. Add actual insertion fees or listing upgrades you want the sale to recover. For an attributed General campaign sale, enter the percentage charged for that listing. The calculator applies it to the modeled checkout total. Check your advertising report for the actual attribution. Worked example: selling a $100 item on eBay Fictional sale in a supported 13.6% basic category with an attributed 4% ad Order line Calculation Amount Seller revenue $100 item + $8 buyer-paid shipping $108.00 Buyer checkout $108 + 6% tax $114.48 Final value percentage $114.48 × 13.6% $15.57 Per-order fee Checkout exceeds $10 $0.40 Attributed ad $114.48 × 4% $4.58 Seller costs $48 item + $10 postage + $2 supplies + $3 allowance $63.00 Contribution $108 less modeled fees and costs $24.45 With the same price and no attributed ad fee, contribution rises to $29.03. To model $25 contribution with the 4% ad still attributed, the item price must reach $100.68. Keep the shipping assumption and tax treatment consistent before comparing prices. What changes near the $10 and $7,500 thresholds? At $9.50 plus 6% tax and no shipping, the checkout total is $10.07. The order therefore uses the $0.40 charge. A small price increase at the threshold can reduce what you keep temporarily, because the fixed charge jumps by $0.10. The target-price calculation checks both sides. On the 13.6% schedule, an $8,000 fee base uses 13.6% on the first $7,500 and 2.35% on the remaining $500. That gives $1,031.75 in percentage fees before the order fee. Applying 13.6% to all $8,000 would overstate the modeled fee. Model an eligible electronically delivered eBay item Check eBay’s electronically delivered items policy before choosing a listing format. For sellers without approval, eBay directs covered listings to the Information Products classified-ad format. Policy exceptions and approval requirements depend on the product. Choose Digital product to estimate a one-sale scenario without shipping. Enter only the percentage, fixed, listing and advertising charges that actually apply to the format. For a classified listing using a separate payment method, allocate any applicable classified listing cost and enter the processor’s verified fees on the stated buyer-total basis. Check the actual category and order before choosing a price Find the category in the listing and verify whether your Store subscription changes its rate. Choose only a supported preset or a confirmed single flat-rate schedule. Use the shipping amount eBay uses in the fee base. Expedited and international options can have exceptions. If your order needs separate fee bases, use the eBay statement instead of this model. Compare your fee statement, ad attribution and net order proceeds. Treat monthly Store cost, fee credits and multi-item checkouts as separate reconciliation items. Assumptions and limits One item and one order on eBay US in USD. Physical orders use standard domestic shipping. For an eligible digital sale, only entered fees apply. Rates cover the selected basic category schedules only. The model excludes Store-specific tiered rates, special categories, international fees, account surcharges, multi-item checkouts and exact refund credits. Contribution is before overhead and income tax. Frequently asked questions How much does eBay take from a $100 sale? The worked example uses $8 buyer-paid shipping, 6% tax, a 13.6% category fee and an attributed 4% ad. The modeled eBay fees are $20.55 before seller costs. Changing category, shipping, tax or advertising changes the answer. Does eBay charge final value fees on sales tax? The US basic fee schedule uses a total sale amount including applicable sales tax and other covered amounts. The tax is excluded from seller revenue in the profit calculation. Is the eBay order fee $0.30 or $0.40? Under the modeled basic schedule it is $0.30 at a total sale amount of $10 or less and $0.40 above $10. Some special category rules differ. Can I estimate fees for an eBay digital product? Yes, for an eligible listing. Switch to Digital product and enter verified fees for its listing and payment format. The digital estimate excludes shipping and does not use the physical category fee schedule. Can I use this for my eBay Store rate? Use the custom percentage only if the official schedule you verified is a single flat percentage and the rest of the modeled charges apply. Store tiers with different thresholds require a separate reconciliation. Then use the examples below to reconcile proceeds with your order costs. Payment details US merchant fee schedule Choose a fee schedule PayPal Checkout · 3.49 % + $0.49 Send/Receive Money for Goods and Services · 2.99 % + $0.00 PayPal QR code transaction · 2.29 % + $0.09 Custom fee Calculation Estimate seller proceeds Find the charge for a target net Gross payment (USD) Estimated seller proceeds Choose the fee schedule that matches how you receive the payment. What this calculator includes US domestic USD payment presets Editable custom rate and fixed fee Forward fee estimates and reverse charge calculation Choose the fee that matches your PayPal transaction Start with the transaction type and fee on your PayPal activity or statement. Choose Checkout for a matching Checkout payment, Send/Receive Money for Goods and Services for that named transaction type, or QR for a matching QR transaction. Use Custom when your contract or payment product shows different terms. At $100, the displayed Checkout preset estimates $3.98 in fees and $96.02 in proceeds. The Goods and Services preset estimates $2.99 and $97.01. These are separate transaction types. Check the actual payment record before applying either rate to a forecast. Worked example: receive $100 after a 3% fee plus $0.30 Select Custom fee, enter 3 and 0.30, then select Find the charge for a target net and enter $100. The result is $103.40 gross. The modeled fee rounds to $3.40, leaving $100.00. A $103.39 charge leaves $99.99, so it misses the target by a cent. Use the result as a pricing estimate. Before changing what a buyer is charged, check the terms for your payment product and any rules that apply to your pricing. Reconcile payment proceeds with order profit Suppose a $100 payment under the same custom rate includes $8 collected for sales tax. PayPal proceeds in the model are $96.70. Set aside the $8 tax and deduct $60 of product, shipping and packaging costs to get $28.70 contribution before overhead. If your order report already deducts the payment fee, do not deduct it a second time. Fixed fees make small payments comparatively expensive. At the same custom rate, a $5 payment costs $0.45 (9%), while a $100 payment costs $3.30 (3.3%). Use effective fee rate to compare order sizes, and use the statement to reconcile actual fees. How PayPal fees affect seller proceeds Transaction fee is the gross USD payment multiplied by the selected percentage plus the fixed fee. We round the total fee to cents and subtract it from the gross payment. Use the total amount PayPal processes, including any shipping or taxes included in the customer payment. At a custom 3% plus $0.30, a $100 payment has a $3.30 estimated fee and leaves $96.70. Reverse mode checks the cent-denominated result against that same forward formula. The preset table was checked on November 28, 2026. Select the named product only when it matches how you receive the payment. For other products or contracted pricing, enter your verified rate under Custom. Assumptions and limits US domestic merchant payments received in USD. Estimates follow the displayed rates and rounding model. Account-specific pricing, FX, international add-ons, disputes, refunds, transfers and payout fees are outside these presets. Frequently asked questions What amount do I enter? Enter the gross amount processed by PayPal, or switch to target net to calculate the minimum gross charge under the selected fee model. Why can the estimated fee differ from my statement? The product, account terms, currency and additional charges can affect the final fee. Compare the selected rate and fee basis with your PayPal statement. What is the difference between PayPal Checkout and Send/Receive Money for Goods and Services? PayPal lists them as separate domestic commercial transaction types. Choose the exact type used for the payment. documents.text: Business Depreciation Calculator Published November 28, 2026 Compare straight-line and double-declining depreciation for a business asset. See the yearly expense, accumulated depreciation and closing book value, then download the Excel schedule. Asset details Asset cost (USD) Residual value (USD) Useful life (full years) Book depreciation method Straight-line Double-declining balance Annual book depreciation schedule Expense is rounded to cents, and the final year allocates the remaining amount above residual. Total depreciation $10,000.00 · Final book value $2,000.00 Year Opening book value Annual expense Accumulated depreciation Closing book value 1 $12,000.00 $2,000.00 $2,000.00 $10,000.00 2 $10,000.00 $2,000.00 $4,000.00 $8,000.00 3 $8,000.00 $2,000.00 $6,000.00 $6,000.00 4 $6,000.00 $2,000.00 $8,000.00 $4,000.00 5 $4,000.00 $2,000.00 $10,000.00 $2,000.00 Download the editable depreciation schedule (.xlsx) What this calculator includes Straight-line and double-declining balance Annual opening, expense, accumulated depreciation and closing balances Editable Excel schedule using the same calculation Gather cost, residual value and useful life Start with the capitalized cost in the asset record, including any qualifying costs already recorded to get the asset ready for use. Enter estimated residual value at the end of the useful life. Use your expected years of business use for the book schedule. If residual equals cost, there is no depreciable amount. Use Straight-line for a steady allocation before rounding. Use Double-declining balance to see a larger expense earlier in the life of the asset. Both schedules allocate the same total cost above residual in this model. Worked example: compare both methods on a $12,000 asset Enter $12,000 cost, $2,000 residual and five years. Straight-line gives $2,000 expense and $10,000 closing book value in year one. Double-declining applies a 40% rate to the $12,000 opening value, giving $4,800 expense and $7,200 closing book value. In year two, double-declining applies 40% to $7,200. Expense is $2,880 and the year closes at $4,320. By year five, both methods have recorded $10,000 in total depreciation and close at $2,000. The schedule stops charging expense once it reaches the residual floor. Check the schedule before using it in your books Check that each opening balance matches the previous closing balance and that opening value minus annual expense equals closing value. At the bottom, original cost should equal final book value plus accumulated depreciation. Download the Excel workbook and enter the same cost, residual, useful life and method on the Inputs sheet. Compare the first-year expense and final balance with the calculator. If your financial year requires a part-year charge, use the linked straight-line guide to see a partial-period example before posting. How the annual book schedule works Straight-line divides cost less residual by useful life. Double-declining applies twice the straight-line rate to each year’s opening book value. Both methods cap expense at the amount above residual and round the expense to cents. In the last year this schedule allocates the remaining amount above residual. It does not automatically switch methods in earlier years. For a $12,000 asset with $2,000 residual and five years of life, straight-line gives $2,000 each year and finishes at $2,000. Assumptions and limits Illustrative full-year book depreciation for one business asset. Partial-year conventions, tax recovery schedules, impairment, disposals and changes in estimates require separate treatment. Frequently asked questions How is accumulated depreciation calculated? Add each year’s depreciation through the end of the selected year. It also equals starting asset cost minus closing book value. Can book value fall below the residual value? This schedule limits depreciation to the amount above residual. The final year brings closing book value to the entered residual. Does the calculator calculate tax depreciation? Use this schedule for book planning. It does not calculate MACRS, tax allowances or partial-year conventions. Use detailed crew planning or the original quick estimate; each mode keeps independent inputs. Results update in your browser as you type. Enter monthly totals for overhead, owner pay and target profit; enter direct costs per job separately. Average price per job $ Net revenue per defined unit after discounts. Exclude taxes collected for others. Materials / product cost per job $ Materials or product consumed per unit, using compatible quantities and purchase costs. Direct labor per job $ Labor that changes with a delivered unit. Keep guaranteed payroll in fixed costs and owner compensation once. Travel + equipment use per job $ Other sale-dependent costs, including flat fees. Exclude the percentage fee entered below. Lead generation cost per booked job $ Acquisition cost allocated per modeled sale. Do not charge a one-time customer cost to every repeat visit. Monthly operating overhead $ Monthly commitments for this operating range, excluding costs already entered per unit. Monthly owner pay $ Monthly owner-compensation requirement. Do not repeat the same owner wage in per-unit labor. Target monthly profit $ Additional monthly profit goal beyond entered costs and owner pay. Zero means no additional profit goal. Payment and platform fees % Percentage of selling price. A flat transaction charge belongs in other variable cost. Active team members Positive whole team size contributing the modeled productive hours. Hours per team member / week hrs Available hours per team member per week before productive-utilization adjustment. Delivery hours per job hrs Total worker-hours per completed unit, including necessary preparation, delivery and allocated travel. Productive utilization % Share of available hours usable for the modeled delivery work. Do not subtract the same downtime twice. Inquiry-to-job conversion % Completed sales divided by comparable qualified inquiries. Enter a measured rate above zero.
